Staff provided an overview of the Open House setup and materials, and presented the initial results from the Prioritization Activity Boards and Strategies by Chapter Boards. Staff highlighted the highest-earning long and short term strategies, as well as the chapter strategies that received the highest amount of star stickers. Chair Polski thanked Planning Staff and the Planning Board for their level of effort on this project, and expressed a desire to ensure the Planning Board could have conversations and hear each other’s opinions and comments. Board Member Huntsberry asked if Staff could intake all the feedback from Board members and aggregate the information and provide it back out to the Board. Board Member Huntsberry shared he was surprised by the support for the zoning changes, and Chair Polski noted the support for housing. Board Member Guzman Stokes appreciated the breakout of feedback showing different methods of analysis. Board Member Huntsberry shared his appreciation for Interface’s process. e) Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Commission – No Report. VI. Adjournment – The meeting was adjourned at 6:57 pm. Page 3 of 3 Staff Report to the Planning Board ITEM A Meeting: Application #: September 14, 2026 Continued to October 5th, 2026 PLN-26-8 All application materials available online, linked here Application Type: Project Name: Location: Minor Subdivision with Unified Development Review Minor Subdivision – Free Chapel of St. John the Evangelist 59 Washington Street includes properties with mailing addresses 61 & 63 Poplar Street Plat/Lot: Zone: Applicant Plat 12, Lot 120 R-10 Residential Zabriskie Memorial Church of St. John the Evangelist Project Description: Application of Zabriskie Memorial Church of St. John the Evangelist, for a Minor Subdivision with dimensional variances of TAP 12, Lot 120 to be considered under Unified Development Review. The applicant proposes to subdivide an existing lot consisting of 40,083 square feet of land area into two lots, with Proposed Lot 1 consisting of 8,500 square feet of land, and the existing structure of a single-family residence known as the “Dennis House” and Proposed Lot 2 consisting of 31,583 square feet of land with the existing Church, Guild House, and multi-family structure. The applicant is requesting dimensional variances from R-10 Zoning code sections regarding minimum lot area, setback requirements, lot coverage requirements, and parking space standards. Details on the requested variances are listed below. I. Background a. Variance(s) Requested: 1. Dimensional Variances: • 17.20.030– Minimum Lot Area. To allow Proposed Lot 1 to be 8,500 square feet of land area where 10,000 square feet is required. • 17.20.040 – Setback Requirements. To allow the existing building on Proposed Lot 1 to be 11.88 feet from the Washington Street front property line where 15 feet is required, and 7.2 feet from the northside setback where 10 feet is required. • 17.20.040 – Setback Requirements. To allow the existing building on Proposed Lot 2 to be .49 feet from the Poplar Street front property line, 4.2 feet from the Willow street front property line where 15 feet is required; and, .71 feet from the east side setback where 10 feet is required. 1 Staff Report to the Planning Board ITEM A • 17.20.050 – Lot Coverage Requirements. To allow 22% lot coverage on Proposed Lot 1 where 20% is allowed. • 17.20.050 – Lot Coverage Requirements. To allow 40% lot coverage on Proposed Lot 2 where 20% is allowed. • 17.104.020 – Parking Space Standards. To allow Proposed Lot 2 to have 0 parking spaces where 111 are required. b. Findings of Fact: 1. The subject lot is a conforming lot of record containing 40,083 square feet of land. 2. The subject lot is within the R-10 Residential Zoning District. The R-10 residential district is characterized as an area of medium density residential development. The district’s intent is to provide a transition area of diminishing residential densities, and to maintain a minimum lot size requirement to limit future subdivisions. (Newport, RI - Code of Ordinances, Section 17.20.010 – Legislative intent.) 3. The subject lot is within the local Historic District. 4. The subject lot is within The Point neighborhood. See neighborhood description in Section III. 5. The current use of the subject lot includes the campus and church building for St. John the Evangelist Episcopal church, a single family residence at 59 Washington Street, a multifamily residential building at 63 Poplar Street, and the Guild Hall at 61 Poplar Street. 6. There have been several communications resulting from direct abutter notice as of September 29th, 2026. 7. The subject lot has a future land use of Medium Density Residential (MDR). Within the Comprehensive Plan, Medium Density Residential is described as including “areas with residential lots between the sizes of 10,000 and 20,000 square feet.” (Page 3-15). 8. Previous Actions: • Applicant previously applied with Proposed Lot 1 containing 10,000 square feet of land area. c. Staff Recommendation CONSIDERATION of the Variances requested. See Section VI of this report for more details on the Staff recommendation. CONSIDERATION of the Minor Subdivision, Preliminary Plan requested.
